cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to Timothy, the one he calls his beloved child (2 Timothy 1:1-2). And this next part is NOT a "hey, quick favor" text. Paul charges Timothy in the presence of God and of Christ Jesus, in view of His appearing and His kingdom.

cards.question: Paul charges Timothy in the presence of God and of Christ Jesus. What does Paul say Christ Jesus will do?

answers.text: Judge the living and the dead
Count every star in the sky

cards.text: So what's the charge? No warm-up, no "hope this letter finds you well," just three words: preach the word.

cards.question: Paul tells Timothy to be prepared in season and out of season. What does Paul mean?

answers.text: Ready when it's easy and when it's not
Ready only during the feast days
Ready only when someone asks him

cards.question: Paul tells Timothy to reprove and rebuke people, but to leave the encouraging to someone else.

cards.text: Then Paul tells him why: a time is coming when people won't tolerate sound doctrine. Not skip it now and then, friend, won't TOLERATE it.

cards.question: When people won't tolerate sound doctrine, what does Paul say they'll do instead?

answers.text: Gather teachers to suit their own desires
Stop listening to any teachers at all
Leave the cities and go live alone

cards.text: Paul says they'll do it with itching ears. That's like asking five coworkers if you should buy the thing until somebody FINALLY says yes.

cards.question: Paul says people who gather teachers like that will turn their ears away from the truth. What will they turn aside to?

cards.text: Then Paul swings right back to Timothy with two words: But you. Whatever those itching ears end up doing, Timothy's got WORK to do.

cards.question: Paul tells Timothy to steer clear of hardship so he can keep on preaching.
Paul tells Timothy to be sober in all things, do the work of an evangelist and ___ his ministry.

cards.text: Then the letter gets personal. Paul says he is already being poured out like a drink offering, and the time of his departure is at hand.

cards.question: Looking back, Paul says he has fought the good fight, finished the race and kept the faith. What is he telling Timothy about his life?

answers.text: He stayed faithful all the way to the end
He wishes he had done much more for God
He is ready to start his work all over

cards.text: Friend, the only race I ever finished was hopping to the oven before the timer, and on a gold base, that is NOT fast. Paul's looking past the finish line, though: the crown of righteousness is laid up for him.

cards.question: Paul says the crown of righteousness will be awarded on that day by the Lord, the righteous ___.
Paul says the crown of righteousness is waiting for him and for him alone.

cards.text: That crown goes to all who crave His appearing. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer waiting for that drawer to open, so craving that day? I GET it.

findings.problem: This fill in the blank asks the baker to guess Paul's exact verb in a letter, not his meaning. Nothing on the earlier cards points to fulfill over defend or share, so the right pick comes down to luck.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The blank tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
